ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, general partners, shareholders with a stake equal to or above 25%, and authorized signatories against (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists under Regulations (EC) 2580/2001 and (EU) 269/2010, as amended, (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list, (iii) the OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists applying the OFAC 50-percent-rule methodology to the extent USD clearing, correspondent banking or US touchpoints are contemplated, and (iv) domestic designations published by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier). PEP identification follows FATF Recommendations 12, 22 and 24 and CSSF Circular 19/739. Enhanced due diligence, including notarized source-of-wealth documentation and certified translations, is mandatory where a UBO is a politically exposed person, a senior official, or an entity controlled by a state-owned enterprise, and continuous transaction and ownership monitoring applies after incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – official portal of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS): https://www.lbr.lu, including the electronic publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory filings and the registered corporate name must be entered in the RCS in French (German and Luxembourgish are also admissible in practice; Latin script is mandatory). Non-Latin script names, including Chinese brand names used by the hotpot restaurant chain, must be transliterated into a recognisable Latin-alphabet form for the statutory RCS name, while the Chinese-character trade identity should be separately protected as a Benelux Office for Intellectual Property (BOIP) or EUIPO trademark. The statutory name of an SCSp must include the suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'. The registered name must not conflict with an existing RCS entry or a prior Benelux/EU trademark, must not mislead the public as to the nature, form or regulated status of the business, and must not contravene Luxembourg public policy or decency.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: banque / bank / caisse / financial institution (prior CSSF or Ministry of Finance authorization required)
assurance / insurance / réassurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) authorization required)
état / state / gouvernement / municipal / commune (implies sovereign or public authority; prohibited without ministerial authorization)
université / university / académie (reserved for public-law or specifically authorized institutions)
avocat / lawyer / barreau (reserved for members of the Luxembourg Bar; prohibited for a commercial partnership vehicle)
commissaire / réviseur d'entreprises / auditeur (reserved for certified statutory auditors registered with the CSSF or the Institut Luxembourgeois des Réviseurs d'Entreprises)
SICAV / SICAF / fonds d'investissement / OPC / FCP (requires prior CSSF authorization as an undertaking for collective investment; unavailable to an unregulated SCSp)
bourse / stock exchange / Euronext / Luxembourg Stock Exchange (implies regulated market operator status; prohibited without regulatory recognition)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection of the proposed name by the RCS registrar, the applicant may (i) refile with revised name variants within 15 days of the refusal notice, addressing the stated conflicts and attaching the original refusal letter; and (ii) if the refusal is maintained, file a judicial appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) through a Luxembourg-registered avocat under the procedure applicable to decisions of the Trade and Companies Register under the amended Law of 19 December 2002. The appeal must be introduced within two months of notification of the final refusal, must exhibit the refusal decision, the proposed corrected name, proof of updated availability searches, and the power of attorney of the appellant. The rejected applicant may also request administrative review by the Ministry of Justice where the refusal rests on public policy grounds. Appeals costs are borne by the applicant unless the tribunal reverses the decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A stand-alone virtual mailbox with no physical Luxembourg presence is not permissible for a bankable SCSp engaged in overseas investment intermediation such as the proposed hotpot restaurant holding structure. The SCSp may lawfully use a licensed domiciliation agent regulated under the amended Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, provided the registered office is a physical address in Luxembourg, the domiciliation agreement and its terms are disclosed in the RBE, and commercial substance is demonstrable in the form of local general-partner decision-making, books and records held in Luxembourg, and adequate substance documentation for tax residence. A pure virtual office arrangement would fail bank KYC, tax residence, and letterbox-company risk assessment under CSSF AML/CFT guidance and is therefore rejected for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% over the first 36 months following incorporation. The risk is driven principally by bank on-site KYC and source-of-funds reviews at account opening, substance audits by the Luxembourg tax administration (Administration des contributions directes) under exchange-of-information or letterbox-company inquiries, and targeted inspections following sudden AML red flags; the unregulated SCSp itself is not subject to routine CSSF on-site supervisory visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Book III, Part II, sociétés en commandite simple et spéciale – Articles 608-1 et seq.), and the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the Societe en Commandite Speciale (SCSp)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formal registration application to the RCS accompanied by the executed notarised SCSp partnership agreement and registered-office consent form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for an SCSp; partners determine capital contributions at will and no escrow account is mandated under Luxembourg partnership law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the constitution of the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) under the terms of the partnership agreement is approved. Founding partners irrevocably subscribe to their respective partnership interests and undertake to pay their agreed contributions as recorded in the annexed schedule. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the manager is authorised to execute the lease and to register the partnership. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the partnership manager is appointed to represent the SCSp in all administrative, tax, and commercial dealings, including opening bank accounts, signing regulatory filings and completing necessary licensing applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement before a Luxembourg Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the SCSp partnership agreement in notarial form, designating the general partner and limited partners, capital accounts, profit-sharing terms, management powers, and registered office address. The notary will verify the legal capacity of partners and the lawful, precise business purpose (hotpot restaurant and condiment supply) and will register the deed in the notarial register.
required_dossiers: Notarised SCSp partnership agreement
Certified identification documents (passport or national ID) of all partners
Written consent of the registered office owner
Recording of capital subscription schedule or signed commitment letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises legal objections, amend the offending clauses, obtain apostilles on foreign partner certificates, and resubmit the corrected deed; if conflict persists, initiate a new regularisation by supplementary notarial instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Luxembourg Banking Account and Capital Arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank or MiFID credit institution in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarised partnership agreement together with valid identification of partners and managers to open a business account in the SCSp's name. Although no paid-up capital is statutorily prescribed, if partners elect to contribute a start-up deposit, deposit it into the account and retain the deposit certificate for RCS and licensing evidence.
required_dossiers: Notarised partnership agreement
Valid passport or national identity card of authorised signatories
Proof of registered office address (lease or consent form)
Beneficial ownership declaration and AML/KYC questionnaire
Tax self-certification (OECD/CRS forms)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial ownership or source-of-funds evidence, provide a detailed declaration of beneficial owners and a current RCS extract once available; if the request is based on formal gaps, coordinate with the relationship officer to complete the documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application through the LBR online portal (www.lbr.lu) or through the notary's electronic transfer. Attach the partnership agreement, registered-office consent, and identification of the manager. The filing officer will review the formal documents and enter the SCSp in the RCS, generating the registration number and a draft extract to be published.
required_dossiers: Notarised or certified copy of the partnership agreement
Identification documents and criminal record extracts of the general partner and manager
Written registered-office consent
Completed RCS standard form signed by the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or deficiency notice, correct the flagged points, such as missing translations or incomplete manager identification, within the 15-day deadline and refile electronically without additional fee; any substantive changes must be executed by notarial amendment prior to refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Company and Association Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Resa publication office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS admission, the registry will transmit the formal legal notice for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). The notice will contain the SCSp name, form, registered office, manager identity, and corporate purpose. Verify the wording after publication and obtain the authenticated extract.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract/certificate
Proof of publication (notice text) generated by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice is inaccurate, submit a formal correction request to LBR and, if necessary, execute a rectifying notarial deed to be republished; delay costs are borne by the SCSp only if the error is attributable to the filer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Business Establishment Licence under the Law of 2 September 2011
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des classes moyennes (DCM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a complete establishment licence dossier for the hotpot restaurant activity through the Ministry's Guichet.lu portal, incorporating the RCS extract, criminal record excerpts, proof of professional qualification or appointment of a qualified manager, and a floor plan of the premises. The DCM also coordinates with the Food Safety Administration and the municipal administration.
required_dossiers: RCS extract of the SCSp
Criminal record certificate(s) for the manager and general partner
Evidence of professional competence or degreed food-service qualification
Restaurant premises floor plan, sanitation layout and ownership/lease documents
Menu and food-processing description for hygiene review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the Ministry signal an intention to refuse or require supplementary information, submit written observations and cure the identified gap (e.g. professional qualification, sanitation map or lease document) within the stated period; an unfavourable decision may be appealed before the Administrative Tribunal within three months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des classes moyennes; co-administered by the Administration de la sécurité alimentaire (ASD)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Establishment Permit) and Food Business Operator Authorisation (enregistrement de l'exploitant du secteur alimentaire)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – A full EIA report may be required for restaurants with a floor area exceeding 500 m² or a service capacity above 500 meals per day; smaller establishments are subject to prior notification / environmental registration exemptions under the grand-ducal regulation of 21 November 2018
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must align with municipal sewer limits (e.g. maximum 25 mg/l BOD5; 35 mg/l TSS; fats, oils, and grease removed via the grease interceptor); culinary smoke and odours must be filtered in conformity with the 2011 establishment-regulation and ITM specification S/024 on kitchen ventilation; VOC emissions from condiment production, if any, must remain under 1.5 kg/hour per source smoke-abatement threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) after inspection of kitchen hood suppression, gas-lines and escape routes; structural load certification from CITI-LABO confirming floor adequacy for heavy kitchen equipment; workplace occupational clearance by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) for electrical safety, ventilation and fire extinguishing equipment prior to opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des Douanes et Accises for customs and excise; registration and publication effected through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) platform (www.lbr.lu) and the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-established SCSp must appoint a Luxembourg-based authorised representative, file the constitutive deed (notarised) with the RCS via the LBR electronic portal, obtain the RCS business registration number (B number), and receive a national identification number (matricule) assigned by the ACD. VAT registration is then filed with the AEDT on Form 640 (for non-resident taxable persons) or Form 640G (for Luxembourg-established companies), producing a LUXXXXXXXXX VAT identification number valid for EU-recognised transactions; the entire process typically completes within 10–20 business days using an apostilled certificate of incorporation, partnership agreement, and proof of registered address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory default under the Luxembourg partnership law of 12 July 2013: no corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at the SCSp level, with partners assessed on their distributive share. No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists in Luxembourg domestic law; however, express transparency is confirmed in the partnership agreement, and a partner may make a US Form 8832 classification election for US federal tax purposes. An optional election to constitute a VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 63 of the Luxembourg VAT Law is available for closely linked entities, and hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD (law of 21 December 2017) may be elected or documented to neutralise double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg-established taxable persons carrying out supplies above EUR 35,000 annual turnover are mandatorily VAT-registered; below that threshold, the small business exemption may apply absent a waiver. Non-resident entities (including an SCSp) that undertake any taxable transaction in Luxembourg, regardless of turnover, are subject to compulsory VAT registration on a reverse-charge or direct-liability basis; a foreign SCSp holding an overseas hotpot restaurant and condiment supply chain will generally have no Luxembourg VAT registration unless it imports goods for resale, engages in Luxembourg establishment, or derivatively registers to exercise EU VAT recovery rights.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time transactional clearance or digital stamping obligation exists; Luxembourg applies the EU invoicing directive (2010/45/EU) permitting PDF/e-invoices with advanced electronic signatures or EDI under mutual agreement. Mandatory Peppol-based B2G e-invoicing applies to suppliers invoicing Luxembourg public authorities through the national e-Facturation platform. All VAT returns, recapitulative statements (European Sales List), Intrastat filings, and periodic listings must be submitted electronically via MyGuichet.lu (eTVA module) or a certified EDI channel; no continuous transaction control systems or automated hourly fiscal reporting are in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of goods to non-EU destinations is zero-rated under Article 50 of the Luxembourg VAT Law where the exporter proves delivery outside the EU and is identified as the exporter on the customs export declaration; intra-EU dispatches of condiment products to a VAT-registered customer are zero-rated under Article 41 subject to valid EU VAT numbers and ESL reporting. Services physically performed offshore (including catering operations and overseas hotpot restaurant management fees) fall outside the Luxembourg territorial scope and are excluded from Luxembourg VAT. The invoice must include the customer's and supplier's VAT numbers, the zero-rated 'Article 50' reference, and be supported by transport and payment evidence retained for a minimum of ten years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration (SAD/Douane single administrative document) lodged with the Administration des Douanes et Accises via DGCE/presentation to the LU export office
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or airway bill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial invoice with Incoterms clause and proof of title transfer
Packing list and export carrier's certificate of arrival
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidence of payment from the non-EU purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg customs may retroactively deny zero-rating for up to ten years upon incomplete export proof, assessing output VAT at the standard rate plus late-payment interest (EURIBOR + 5 percentage points). Fraudulent claims or forged export documents trigger double taxation penalties (generally 10% to 25% of the evaded tax), criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and possible imprisonment for VAT fraud under the Luxembourg Criminal Code; directors and general partners of the SCSp face joint civil liability for clawed-back VAT, statutory interest, and penalties, alongside potential blacklisting of the operator from the registered exporter scheme.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem; banking supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), while capital movement and exchange control matters are governed by the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the EU Capital Movement Regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Luxembourg applies no exchange controls under EU law, and there are no restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, or partnership distributions from an SCSp. Capital contribution, profit distribution, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred to non-residents, subject only to AML/KYC verification and statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL for transactions exceeding EUR 12,500.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no repatriation deadlines for export receipts. All export proceeds may be retained in any currency, deposited in Luxembourg bank accounts or abroad, and are freely deployable. The only administrative duty is the monthly or quarterly balance-of-payments declaration to the BCL if cumulative cross-border flows exceed the reporting threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (for initial partnership subscriptions) and Operational Account (for ongoing treasury, trade settlement, and payroll)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with dedicated multi-currency capabilities for overseas hotpot restaurant treasury operations
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account; offers integrated SWIFT, cross-currency clearing, and forex lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions under EU payment services rules are viable for low-value operational payments, merchant acquiring, and prepaid cards. However, the SCSp structure with overseas direct-operated restaurants will likely face higher compliance scrutiny due to ownership complexity. EMIs typically cannot provide overdrafts or commercial letters of credit, and may require a partner bank for segregated trust accounts. The core treasury, capital escrow, and trade finance functions should be anchored at a Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Because an SCSp has no legal personality, banks must identify the general partner, the beneficial owners, and the economic settlors. A physical onboarding interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises is expected for a non-resident-owned restaurant investment platform. Remote video identification is accepted under CSSF AML guidelines only if the structure is low risk and all parties are premised in fully compliant jurisdictions. In practice, a notarized power of attorney and a face-to-face meeting with the general partner or its authorized signatories will accelerate onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp used as a pass-through partnership without legal personality, creating uncertainty as to who owns and controls the deposit funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized, non-amortized partnership agreement (contrat de société) and any private deed; certificate of registration (extrait RCS) from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register; a clear legal opinion on the SCSp's capital structure; a full list of general partners and limited partners with beneficial ownership percentages; written UBO declarations consistent with Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 as amended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners residing in a high-risk or non-equivalent AML jurisdiction, increasing the probability of money-laundering screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Banked account statements and source-of-wealth documentation (share purchase agreements, property deeds, employment contracts, audited financial statements); tax residence certificates from all beneficial owners; signed PEP and sanctions self-certifications; independent negative media and litigation checks from a commercial intelligence provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity consisting predominantly of cash-intensive restaurant dining, condiment supply, and POS merchant flows, which may exhibit thin margins and potential under-reporting risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully integrated five-year business plan with sober cash-flow projections; evidence of direct-operated restaurant leases and property proof; POS merchant acquiring and terminal contracts; audited financials of the operating subsidiary in the target country; supply-chain purchase contracts for condiment procurement; and a documented treasury policy separating cash-handling from vendor payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution to the SCSp arriving from related-party offshore companies, causing ambiguity on the true source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unbroken provenance trail from the immediate sender to the ultimate natural-person investor; the initial subscription agreement and capital account statements; board minutes of the SCSp approving the injection and intended use of funds; notarized loan or contribution agreements if structured as shareholder loans; and declaration of the economic rationale for using an SCSp.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed through the SCSp's capital escrow account at the Luxembourg bank. Investors execute a SWIFT MT103 wire with the bank using field 72 (Remittance Information) containing the XML/SWIFT purpose code 'SUBS' (capital subscription) and a clear narrative 'Capital contribution to Société en Commandite Spéciale [RCS number]'. For non-euro investors, the bank will require a spot FX contract converting the subscription amount into EUR. The bank verifies sanctions, source of funds, and the capital escrow instruction letter signed by the general partner. All inbound payments are held until the bank's AML/KYC file is fully cleared and the beneficial ownership declaration is accepted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements from the SCSp to overseas hotpot restaurant operations use SEPA SCT wires for euro-area vendors, SWIFT MT103 for cross-border suppliers and intercompany loans, and commercial letters of credit (UCP 600-documented) issued by the Luxembourg bank for large equipment imports from high-risk or long-lead jurisdictions. For FX cross-currency payments, the bank executes a spot or forward contract with a clear underlying trade invoice. Merchant-acquiring settlement flows from the restaurant's POS terminals are routed into a local operating entity account and consolidated periodically through intercompany loans or dividend payments to the SCSp, respecting transfer-pricing benchmarks for condiment supply procurement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNH (offshore renminbi) non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only when onshore deliverable forwards are unavailable
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for notional refinancing of funded restaurant projects
Vanilla EUR/USD foreign exchange options (puts/calls) for contingent acquisition liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership details (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RBE; Ministry of Justice supervisory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the initial RBE filing; any UBO change requires an update within one month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automated EUR 125 per-infraction notice; criminal fines EUR 125–25,000; persistent failure may trigger prosecutor referral and block official extracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit with the Trade Register (comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via LBR e-filing portal of the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end (calendar-year SCSp by 31 July); small/micro abbreviated formats allowed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine EUR 500–10,000 per managing officer under Article 183 of the Law of 10 August 1915; formal registrar default notice, court-ordered filing with astreinte, and administrative radiation after persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: List of partners (liste des associés) maintained and filed on change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing within one month of any partnership interest transfer or partner admission; no annual re-filing if unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Article 183 fine EUR 500–10,000 on the general partner; inaccurate register can expose the general partner to third-party liability and AML findings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Luxembourg economic substance return (conditional – relevant activities in Luxembourg)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Tax Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual income/corporate tax declaration; calendar-year return due by 30 June (31 December with e-filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Up to EUR 10,000 administrative fine; denial of tax residency and recharacterization of payments otherwise benefiting from substance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax declaration (SCSp transparent return) assessed on partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Tax Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual; calendar-year declaration by 30 June, extended to 31 December when electronically submitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 0.6% monthly on tax due; late-filing penalties up to EUR 10,000; ex officio assessment and potential sanctions on the general partner

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) where the SCSp exceeds two of three criteria for two consecutive years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4M; net turnover EUR 8.8M; average workforce 50. CSSF-regulated fund SCSp may be audited irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, as amended; EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS optional for statutory accounts and mandatory for consolidated statements when used

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation filed electronically on the RBE portal within one month of the RBE registration anniversary; any partnership interest transfer that changes 25%+ ultimate ownership or control must be reported within one month. The confirmation covers all entities registered in the RCS, including the SCSp, and costs EUR 19 per filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (register of limited and general partners)
Register of Directors and general partner (gérant) records
Minute Book (decisions of partners and management)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,200–3,500 per year (approx. USD 1,300–3,800) covering registered office in Luxembourg, RBE/annual-return filings and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 7,000–20,000 (approx. USD 7,600–21,600) for a small-to-mid SCSp when audit is statutory or required by financing stakeholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For Luxembourg-resident companies, the aggregate CIT rate is 24.94% in Luxembourg City. A Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to corporate income tax; profit is allocated and taxed at partner level. Qualifying corporate partners may benefit from the participation exemption (100% exemption for dividends and capital gains) and the IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income). No statutory tax holiday applies to restaurant or catering activities; foreign-source trading income of a non-resident partner without a Luxembourg PE is generally not subject to Luxembourg CIT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg annual direct tax declaration (Form 1 for CIT / Form 2 for non-resident taxpayers) filed electronically through the MyGuichet e-TAX portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Returns are due no later than 31 March of the year following the tax year; for calendar-year taxpayers the ACD usually extends the deadline to 31 December, and further extensions may be requested via the e-TAX portal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp, its registered address, Luxembourg tax number, RCS number, and the names, tax IDs and profit-sharing ratios of all general and limited partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must insert their foreign tax identification number and treaty country of residence, and attach a current tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by that treaty state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The partner's agreed share of the SCSp's net profit or loss for the fiscal year, adjusted for partnership agreement allocations and capital account computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners not carrying on business through a Luxembourg permanent establishment report only the Luxembourg-source portion of their allocation; otherwise the full allocation is taxable in Luxembourg through a PE return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses under the LIR, including hidden profit distributions, excessive management or royalty fees, tax penalties, fines and any non-business expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must apply the same statutory add-backs in proportion to their interest and retain transfer pricing documentation evidencing the arm's-length nature of related-party fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for participation exemption, IP box deduction, notional interest deduction, and any double-tax relief or treaty credits applicable to the partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: These deductions are available primarily to qualifying Luxembourg-resident corporate partners; non-resident partners should apply the corresponding foreign tax credit and treaty articles rather than domestic Luxembourg exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Prepayments, Withholdings and Refund Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable quarterly tax prepayments, Luxembourg withholding taxes suffered, municipal business tax paid, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must attach a formal tax credit computation and source-country tax certificates; refund or credit claims must be filed within the statutory recovery period, generally five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing can lead to administrative fines of up to EUR 500, default interest at 0.6% per month on outstanding tax, an ex officio assessment, and a late-payment surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax. Wilful failure or falsification may trigger criminal sanctions, including imprisonment up to five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Municipal business tax declaration (Taxe d'affaires communale, ICC) filed with the competent Luxembourg commune through the ACD/MyGuichet e-TAX system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed on the same annual cycle as the income tax return; assessments are based on the SCSp's Luxembourg business income and allocable payroll and net wealth within each commune.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of each Luxembourg establishment, including the address of the hotpot restaurant or administrative office, staffing levels and business purpose.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner with no Luxembourg PE but with a resident SCSp carrying on trade must ensure the SCSp's activities are separately declared in the name of the SCSp for ICC purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The taxable ICC profit, computed from the SCSp's commercial and industrial income before income taxes and partner allocations, with statutory add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must refer to the SCSp-level ICC return for their allocation; the ICC is paid at SCSp level and generally credited against partner-level Luxembourg income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportionment of taxable profit among Luxembourg communes based on payroll and asset factors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should verify the allocation methodology because under foreign tax credit rules the ICC is typically creditable against home-state income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or pay municipal business tax triggers the same default interest and surcharge rules as income tax; local communes may issue enforceable collection orders and additional fines for incomplete payroll declarations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% for dividends distributed by a Luxembourg resident company subject to CIT. An SCSp is fiscally transparent; distributions or profit allocations by the SCSp to partners are generally not treated as dividends and therefore are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at the SCSp level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on source-country dividends paid to the SCSp or on Luxembourg-source withholding if a CIT-subject entity is interposed, the beneficial owner must submit a current tax residence certificate (TRC), a written treaty relief declaration, and evidence of satisfaction of the limitation-of-benefits or holding-period clauses to the ACD or paying agent. For a transparent SCSp, the treaty entitlement is assessed at the level of each partner; a non-resident partner must claim treaty benefits under its own residence state's DTA with the source state, not under Luxembourg's DTA, unless the treaty contains a look-through provision. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief may apply where the parent partner is a qualifying EU company with the required minimum shareholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties, so the statutory rate is 0%. Where payments are made to resident associated enterprises in non-cooperative jurisdictions, anti-abuse rules or CFC/GAAR measures may disallow deductions or reclassify income, but no statutory WHT is collected at source. Treaty rates therefore are not relevant because the domestic zero rate is more favourable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are required where the Luxembourg entity's annual related-party transactions reach or exceed EUR 150,000 and the group's consolidated turnover is at least EUR 50 million; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750 million. Even below the threshold, comparable TP documentation must be available on request to support the arm's-length nature of controlled transactions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a separate codified Economic Substance Regulations statute, but substance is enforced through the domestic GAAR (Article 6 LIR), OECD BEPS/ATAD implementation, transfer pricing rules and tax ruling practice. An SCSp claiming Luxembourg tax residence or treaty benefits must demonstrate substantive local economic activity: local management and decision-making, a registered office, employees, bank accounts and audited or prepared accounts. A shell SCSp without these attributes is re-characterised, its tax transparency may be denied, and treaty benefits may be rejected.
